To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) it is possible to recover SKU-level preference parameters from a market share model that is estimated using aggregate data and (2) the recovered preference parameters are more accurate than the preference parameters that can be estimated from the market share model itself.

(a) the parameters of a truly disaggregate model of SKU-level preferences can be obtained by calculation from estimated parameters of an attribute-level model; and (b) the disaggregate parameters are more accurate predictors than the attribute-level parameters.

(1) it is possible to recover SKU-level preference parameters and marketing-mix response coefficients from a store-level market share model estimated on aggregate brands and (2) the resulting SKU-level parameters have superior predictive performance.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the recovery of stockkeeping-unit-level (SKU-level) preferences and response sensitities.
the estimation of a stockkeeping-unit (Sku) preference model using data on market shares and marketing-mix expenditures at the brand level.
the estimation and interpretation of market share models.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
“the approach described in this article is a useful and practical tool for recovering disaggregate parameters from aggregate data.”
the authors have developed a new method of recovering disaggregate parameters from aggregate market share models.
this is an important contribution to the literature on market share modeling, and it is an interesting approach to the estimation of disaggregate models from aggregate data.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the authors show that a disaggregate SKU-level market share model can be recovered from an aggregate attribute-level model, and that the disaggregate model can be estimated more accurately than the disaggregate model.
we show how to recover stockkeeping-unit (or SKU)-level preferences and sensitivities from a market share model estimated on item aggregates.

the proposed approach provides a practical and accurate method for recovering SKU-level preference parameters from aggregate market share models estimated on brand aggregates, without the need to estimate the more complex disaggregate model.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, for a market share model estimated on an aggregate level, it is possible to recover disaggregate parameters by calculation.
it is possible to recover disaggregate-level preference and response sensitivities from aggregate data, provided that disaggregate-level data are available.

, for the case of market share models estimated on item aggregates, it is possible to recover stockkeeping-unit-level preference parameters and response sensitivities by calculation from the attribute-level parameters, thus obviating the need to estimate a more complex disaggregate model.
